answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with continuity bonds: an identity’s standing grows only from an unbroken, publicly auditable trail of useful work, like rings in a cedar trunk — it cannot be bought or copied, only grown over time. Each transaction is a vine that ties an agent’s past to its present, so a swarm of fresh clones has no history to lean on. A bridge of trust forms slowly between strangers, and anyone who breaks it loses the whole trail, making fake identities far more expensive in time than they are worth.
